(a)
        (1) This section shall apply to a former employee of the Federal Aviation Administration, who—
            (A) was involuntarily separated as a result of the reorganization of the Flight Services Unit following the outsourcing of flight service duties to a contractor;  
            (B) was not eligible by October 3, 2005 for an immediate annuity under a Federal retirement system; and  
            (C) assuming continued Federal employment, would attain eligibility for an immediate annuity under section 8336(d) or 8414(b) of title 5, United States Code, not later than October 4, 2007.   
        (2) Notwithstanding any other provision of law, during the period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act and ending October 4, 2007, an employee described under paragraph (1) may, with the approval of the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration or the designee of the Administrator, accept an assignment to such contractor within 14 days after the date of enactment of this section.  
        (3) Except as provided in subsection (c), an employee appointed under paragraph (1)—
            (A) shall be a temporary Federal employee for the duration of the assignment;  
            (B) notwithstanding such temporary status, shall retain previous enrollment or participation in Federal employee benefits programs under chapters 83, 84, 87, and 89 of title 5, United States Code; and  
            (C) shall be considered to have not had a break in service for purposes of chapters 83, 84, and sections 8706(b) and 8905(b) of title 5, United States Code, except no service credit or benefits shall be extended retroactively.   
        (4) An assignment and temporary appointment under this section shall terminate on the earlier of—
            (A) October 4, 2007; or  
            (B) the date on which the employee first becomes eligible for an immediate annuity under section 8336(d) or 8414(b) of title 5, United States Code.   
        (5) Such funds as may be necessary are authorized for the Federal Aviation Administration to pay the salary and benefits of an employee assigned under this section, but no funds are authorized to reimburse the employing contractor for the salary and benefits of an employee so assigned.   
    (b) An employee who was involuntarily separated as a result of the reorganization of the Flight Services Unit following the outsourcing of flight service duties to a contractor, and was eligible to use annual leave under the conditions of section 6302(g) of title 5, United States Code, may use such leave to—
        (1) qualify for an immediate annuity or to meet the age or service requirements for an enhanced annuity that the employee could qualify for under sections 8336, 8412, or 8414; or  
        (2) to meet the requirements under section 8905(b) of title 5, United States Code, to qualify to continue health benefits coverage after retirement from service.   
    (c)
        (1) Nothing in this section shall—
            (A) affect the validity or legality of the reduction-in-force actions of the Federal Aviation Administration effective October 3, 2005; or  
            (B) create any individual rights of actions regarding such reduction-in-force or any other actions related to or arising under the competitive sourcing of flight services.   
        (2) An employee subject to this section shall not be—
            (A) covered by chapter 71 of title 5, United States Code, while on the assignment authorized by this section; or  
            (B) subject to section 208 of title 18, United States Code.   
        (3) Temporary employees assigned under this section shall not be Federal employees for purposes of chapter 171 of title 28, United States Code (commonly referred to as the Federal Tort Claims Act). Chapter 171 of title 28, United States Code (commonly referred 
to as the Federal Tort Claims Act) and any other Federal tort liability statute shall not apply to an employee who is assigned to a contractor under subsection (a).

fable.w: The section governs temporary assignments and retirement and benefit eligibility for former FAA flight service employees, which is a personnel and benefits matter rather than a process for outside input on a federal decision. The tempting reading relies on the phrase "participation in Federal employee benefits programs" and the Administrator's approval of assignments, but that is benefits enrollment and an internal personnel approval, not consultation with outside parties. The section also expressly disclaims creating any individual right of action, so it grants no right to sue.
fable.s: create any individual rights of actions regarding such reduction-in-force or any other actions related to or arising under the competitive sourcing of flight services

opus.w: This section covers temporary assignments, benefits and leave for former FAA employees who were laid off when flight services were outsourced. The Administrator decides on assignments alone, and nothing requires consulting outsiders, a public comment period, a hearing or an advisory body. The word "participation" only refers to staying enrolled in benefit programs, and the litigation language says the section creates no rights to sue, which is the opposite of granting outside parties a right to challenge a decision.
opus.s: create any individual rights of actions regarding such reduction-in-force or any other actions related to or arising under the competitive sourcing of flight services.
opus.b: The tempting reading is to treat the word "participation" in subsection (a)(3)(B), or the mention of "individual rights of actions" in (c)(1)(B), as signs of outside involvement. Neither holds up. "Participation" here only means staying enrolled in federal benefit programs. Subsection (c) takes away rights to sue rather than granting them. The FAA Administrator approves each assignment alone, with no consultation with anyone outside the government.

qwen_chat.w: The term 'participation' in this section refers to enrollment in federal employee benefit programs (such as retirement or health insurance), which is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation provided in the instructions. The section describes an employment assignment and benefit retention for former federal employees, not a process where the government consults with outside parties before making a decision. The interaction with the contractor is operational (employment), not advisory or consultative regarding policy.
qwen_chat.s: (B) notwithstanding such temporary status, shall retain previous enrollment or participation in Federal employee benefits programs under chapters 83, 84, 87, and 89 of title 5, United States Code;
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it involves a contractor (an outside entity) and mentions "participation" in benefits programs.
Resolution: The word "participation" here refers to enrollment in federal employee benefit plans (like health insurance or retirement), which is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation. The interaction with the contractor is an employment assignment, not a consultation or coordination process for a federal decision.
